seal.statement: The partition leader admits a replica (raft ADD of a CREATE_REPLICA/REPLACE target) from an explicit admission request answered from the committed replica operation (operation id, partition, replica identity, target node), never from the target's services row arriving in the leader's CDC-fed SystemTableCache; the committed admission node comes from the operation, not from a row. A routed system-table write answers at commit with its log position; a consumer that needs its own projection waits on that position, ended only by shutdown. Deleted for these decisions: the cache-row admission producer (handleSystemTableCacheChange -> reconcileRaftPeersFromCacheForService -> admitPartitionRaftPeer, its init call and its cache re-read on re-drive) and the cache-visibility wait (waitForCacheUpdate, its 750/250 budget split, the bootstrap bypass, the authoritative repair fallback, allowPendingVisibility). The CDC obligation hold (cdc_committed_acceptance_unknown) and leader-local apply are handed to the CDC D1-D4 owner as a named obligation. On fresh-formation-user-table-routability every replica named by a committed operation is admitted within one request round of its SYNCING commit, with no dependence on cache visibility.

B3: a committed operation row that is ABSENT is terminal for the request (OPERATION_NOT_ADMITTING / operation_absent, request dropped, no re-read). Reason: the coordinator persists the replica_operations row (PENDING) before it dispatches CREATE_REPLICA, so a target can only send ADMIT_REPLICA for an operation whose row already committed; an absent row on a successful authoritative read means the operation was deleted or never belonged to this target, never 'not yet written'. An unsuccessful read is AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE (kept, re-driven).

B4 and C4 (target side): a NOT_LEADER answer's leaderId replaces the target's leaderId; an absent hint nulls it so discovery (resolveLeaderIdFromMetadata / hint) runs on the next cadence tick - an unadmitted learner hears no raft LEADER_CHANGE, so the answer is how it follows a new leader. A response bound to another partition (the leader address named another partition's replica) is answered NOT_LEADER/partition_mismatch with no hint: the target re-discovers. The leader refuses a request of another partition or of bad shape with REQUEST_INVALID {reason: partition_mismatch | request_shape} before keeping anything (C1: a follower keeps only well-formed requests of its own partition). B2: AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE carries the gateway's typed read outcome (CONTROL_PLANE_READ_OUTCOME, as readOutcome; absent when the read threw) beside the error text; retryAfterMs is kept and is PARTITION_SERVICE_DEFAULT.LEARNER_CATCH_UP_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS - the cadence the target actually re-sends on; the target does not consume it (its cadence is the trigger), it informs logs and any other caller. E3: the delivery names its bound, resolveLearnerPromotionProofDeliveryTimeoutMs (MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS), like the sibling proof request.
